The following lemma singles out a slightly better class of singleton
algebraic stacks than the preceding lemma.

Let <MATH_0001> be an algebraic stack. The following are equivalent
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0002> is reduced, locally Noetherian, and <MATH_0003>
is a singleton, and
<STRUCT_0003> there exists a locally finitely presented, surjective, flat morphism
<MATH_0004> where <MATH_0005> is a field.
<STRUCT_0004>

Assume (2) holds. By
Lemma <REF_0001>
we see that <MATH_0001> is reduced and <MATH_0002> is a singleton.
Let <MATH_0003> be a scheme and let <MATH_0004> be a surjective smooth
morphism. Choose a field <MATH_0005> and a locally finitely presented, surjective,
flat morphism <MATH_0006>.
Then <MATH_0007> is an algebraic space
smooth over <MATH_0008>, hence locally Noetherian (see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0002>).
Since <MATH_0009>
is flat, surjective, and locally of finite presentation, we see
that <MATH_0010> is an fppf covering
and we conclude that <MATH_0011> is locally Noetherian
(Descent on Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0003>).
In other words (1) holds.
